prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one production pixel-art animated character sprite sheet for a 2D side-scrolling tactical fan game inspired faithfully by Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker (1974).
Layout: square 1536x1536 canvas, EXACTLY FOUR columns and FOUR rows, 16 cells. Thin pure CYAN #00FFFF guides: exactly FIVE vertical and FIVE horizontal straight lines including every outer border. Pure flat MAGENTA #FF00FF background in every cell. No labels, numbers, text, UI, logos, watermarks or scenery.
Camera: strict orthographic SIDE PROFILE, character facing screen RIGHT in EVERY frame; nose, gaze and feet point right. Full body including hair, hands and boots always visible. Detailed crisp pixel-art clusters, natural adult proportions, restrained 1974 costume palette, not chibi, not 3D render. Same identity, outfit, body scale and fixed ground baseline across all 16 frames. Center the body consistently inside each cell. Keep character and all gestures small enough to leave at least 40 pixels EMPTY magenta between any art and any cyan guide; never crop hands or feet.
Actions, top to bottom, four independently DRAWN phases left to right for each row:
ROW 1 IDLE: four distinct subtle relaxed breathing/weight-shift poses, small shoulder and arm changes, grounded feet, facing right.
ROW 2 MOVE: four visibly DIFFERENT consecutive walking-cycle phases moving RIGHT: column1 CONTACT stride with right leg forward/left back; column2 PASSING pose with feet close and trailing knee lifting; column3 OPPOSITE CONTACT stride with left leg forward/right back; column4 opposite PASSING pose, feet close and right knee lifting. Alternate the near and far leg silhouettes; do not draw four similar extended-stride poses. Arms swing opposite the legs.
ROW 3 INTERACT: four consecutive nonviolent conversation/briefing gestures, arm preparing, extending a hand forward, gently indicating something ahead, then returning. No extra person, no outside object needed.
ROW 4 REACT: four consecutive mild startled reaction and recovery poses: flinch shoulders, bend knees and bring hands close defensively, look cautiously ahead while still right-facing, settle back. NO injury, blood, death, shooting or combat.
Every cell contains one complete independently drawn pose of the SAME character, no duplicates, no blank cells, no extra portraits. Keep clean separation and stable side-profile orientation throughout. This is original reference-informed fan-made sprite art, not copied official artwork.
Character identity and exact costume:
Ramón Gálvez Mena, also known as Vladimir Zadornov, in Peace Walker1974. Mature light-skinned man with slicked-back dark hair graying at the temples, angular stern face, NO eyeglasses. Knee-length brown trench coat worn open over a brown three-piece suit, muted gray-green collared shirt, dark tie and black dress shoes. His anatomical RIGHT HAND is a distinctive RED mechanical prosthetic with articulated metal fingers; show the red right hand consistently in the visible near arm while he faces RIGHT. The left hand is ordinary flesh, not red. Coat sleeves conceal most forearms. No futuristic armor, no yellow scarf, no helmet, no weapon. Preserve long brown coat and red right hand in all16poses. Interact gestures may use that red hand. This is one identity, not separate Galvez and Zadornov characters.
Visual reference inspected: https://www.konami.com/mg/history/jp/ja/mgspw
CRITICAL CORRECTION: show EXACTLY ONE RED HAND per pose, NEVER two. The visible near arm is his anatomical RIGHT arm with its red prosthetic hand. In ALL16poses keep the ordinary LEFT arm and hand entirely OCCLUDED behind his torso/coat (or concealed inside the coat pocket); do not draw that far hand at all. Only the red RIGHT hand performs every interaction and startled gesture. Even when startled, raise only that single red right hand, never two hands. There must be exactly one visible hand, red, in every frame. Keep the same face, no glasses, brown trench coat and complete four-row action sequence.
reason: Original generation incorrectly showed two red prosthetic hands in some gesture frames; rejected.
